version.changelog: Initial release: methodology skill for designing safe, well-defined agentic loops in Claude Code (six parts, writer/checker split, autonomy ladder, hard-stop gate, command allowlist, proof-run-before-schedule).

llm.summary: This is a safety-oriented planning skill for building supervised recurring agent loops, with no executable installer or hidden payload found.

dimensions.detail: The skill’s stated purpose is to design recurring agent workflows, and its instructions consistently focus on triggers, state files, hard gates, allowlists, proof runs, cost estimates, and supervised autonomy.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: One section tells the agent to ignore unrelated false-positive skill injections; this is framed around irrelevant product-specific hooks, but users should still ensure it never overrides system, security, or platform instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains a single non-executable SKILL.md file and no install scripts, binaries, package hooks, or concealed runtime components.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discusses schedules, hooks, worktrees, cloud routines, commits, pushes, and command allowlists, which are high-impact capabilities but are expected for its purpose and paired with guardrails.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistent state files, scheduled routines, and committed state updates are core to the loop design; the skill emphasizes hard stops, max-iteration backstops, auditability, and human approval before higher autonomy.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want Codex or Claude Code to help build recurring unattended workflows. Before enabling any loop it creates, review the trigger, command allowlist, state file, hard stop, cost estimate, and autonomy level, and keep human approval for pushes, merges, publishing, or destructive actions until the loop has proven itself.
llm.findings:
[SSD-1] expected: The flagged language is a real wording concern because it says to ignore certain mandatory-looking injected skill requests, but artifact context limits it to unrelated product triggers and does not show hidden behavior, exfiltration, or an attempt to bypass safety policy.
[static-scan] expected: Static scan reported no suspicious patterns, consistent with the reviewed artifact being only instructional markdown.
[virustotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean across supplied engines; this supports but does not determine the verdict.
